newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude called lower on consolidation.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude called lower on consolidation.

text.p: NYMEX crude was called lower Tuesday morning, consolidating Monday's run-up and tracking losses in Brent futures on London's IPE, traders said.

"Brent is off in London, and I think we are correcting a bit after rising yesterday on not much of anything. But, the May/June spread is stronger, so that is a postive for the market," said Victor Yu, vice president of Refco Inc.

Crude was called 15 to 20 cents a barrel lower. Heating oil and gasoline were called flat to 0.25 cent a gallon lower. Dealers are also seeking direction from trader estimates of weekly oil inventory data to be released Tuesday evening.
May Brent was off 26 cents at $17.93 a barrel on the IPE.

Preliminary estimates for data to be released by the American Petroleum Institute called for distillate stocks, comprised of heating oil and diesel, and gasoline stocks, each to draw by about two million barrels.
Dealers cited good demand for heating oil due to unseasonably cold weather in the U.S. Northeast while refiners continue to liquidate winter grade gasoline to make room for summer grade.
Crude stocks were seen declining by a similar amount due to increased refinery runs.
On Monday, prices rose on a report that linked Iran to the 1996 bombing of U.S. barracks in Saudi Arabia, but traders said U.S. retaliation, if any, still seems unclear and long term.

"I guess U.S. retaliation seems like maybe a 50/50 chance at this point, and any response seems so far down the road," said a New York crude trader, noting the report has since faded into the background.
On Monday, May crude finished 37 cents up at $19.90 a barrel. May gasoline settled 1.08 cents higher at 61.96 cents a gallon while May heating oil ended up 0.80 cent at 54.67 cents gallon.
